reaction: The final picture usefully connects cell division to both self-renewal and later differentiation.

mostWorthwhile.text: Using the spindle and then actin and myosin was most worthwhile: the planned pictures distinguish separating genomes into nuclei from dividing the cytoplasm.

leastWorthwhile.text: The DNA-copying result was less informative than it could have been: it labels S phase and sister chromatids but does not explain how nucleotides are used to copy DNA.

surprise.text: The spindle result clarified that its assembly occurs during mitosis after DNA copying; it initially has no chromosomes attached.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though combining general new cell proteins with centrosomes simplifies spindle assembly, and the roles of tubulin and the motor protein are not explained.

continue.text: I would choose to continue to see how the daughter cells become different tissues; the final branching diagram sets up that transition clearly.
